brief: The Fed delivered a 25bp hike with a hawkish tone. The vote was unanimous, the new dot plot signals another hike this year, with 4 participants open to hiking at every remaining meeting. Warsh said growth remains very strong and inflation has not made sufficient progress, so the Fed will lean against both. Strong retail sales pushed Q3 GDP estimates higher, and the Fed raised its growth forecast while cutting its year-end unemployment projection to 4.1% from 4.3%. Siegel expects the next hike in December, not October, to avoid pre-midterm political controversy. He treats the 10-year Treasury near 5% (TIPS near 2.6%) as competition for equities: a 20x multiple implies a 5% real earnings yield, a 2.4-point premium over TIPS. Equities can grind higher below 5% but struggle if yields clear it decisively, with no near-term upside catalyst unless yields retreat or energy-driven geopolitical pressure eases. Warsh attributed rising yields to growth, AI investment, and geopolitical inflation, not the deficit, an omission Siegel calls notable. He doubts hikes will derail AI investment despite $15tn in rate-linked loans, flags AI-driven memory and chip inflation, expects an eventual productivity payoff, and is watching money and credit growth as tightening's real test.
